description: Demolition of the existing warehouse building and construction of nine three-storey dwelling houses (9 x 4-bedroom) (Use Class C3) together with associated landscaping, provision of refuse and bicycle storage facilities and rooftop amenity spaces.
decision_conditions:
The proposed development fails to provide sufficient justification
for the total loss of employment workspace on non-designated employment land
without first exploring a mixed-use scheme. Therefore, the principle of
development has not been established contrary to Policy 28 of the Waltham
Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

The proposed rear boundary treatment fails to sufficiently protect
the proposed dwellings from overlooking, due to the proposed boundary treatment
not being consistent with the gradient of Warley Close contrary to Policy 57 of
the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

Due to the close proximity of the existing rear residential
neighbouring buildings, the first and second floor bedroom windows within the
proposed dwelling(s) would have a detrimental impact on the privacy to the
residential occupiers of Units 8 and 9 Lea Park Trading Estate contrary to Policy
57 of the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

Due to a lack of information relating to the non-provision of
existing and proposed streetscene elevations, the application as submitted fails
to adequately demonstrate the impact of the proposed boundary treatment on entrance
to the application site in relation to the existing streetscene contrary to Policy
53 of the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

Due to insufficient information relating to the received daylight
and sunlight report not taking into consideration the impact to rooflights of buildings
within the Lea Park Trading Estate. The application as submitted fails to
adequately demonstrate that the proposed three storey buildings would not have
an unreasonable amenity impact to all of the rear buildings contrary to Policy 57
of the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

No justification has been provided regarding the proposed
departure from the housing mix requirements of the Local Planning Authority,
contrary to Policy 15 of the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

In the absence of a satisfactory Outline Construction
Logistic Plan, a full assessment of how the proposed development would be
built or serviced without severely affecting the public highway could not be
made in accordance with Policies T7 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy 65 of
the Waltham Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

The application as submitted, comprises of inconsistent
information. The proposed 'typical ground floor layout' plan illustrates
provision for 2No. secure cycle stores within the rear garden of each property.
Whereas the Planning and Transport Statement(s) make reference to the site
having 3 long-term and 2 short-term spaces. The application as submitted therefore
fails to adequately demonstrate that there would be sufficient secure parking
storage contrary to Appendix 1 - Parking Standards and Policy 61 of the Waltham
Forest Local Pan Part 1 (2024).

The furthest proposed dwellinghouses houses from the main entrance
exceeds a 60m walking distance from the communal refuse and recycling
storage, this is contrary to the Waste & Recycling Policy for Developers
(2022).

The applicant has failed to provide information of how the communal
refuse and recycling area/ bins would be accessed/ operated by somebody with a disability,
this is contrary to the Waste & Recycling Policy for Developers (2022).

The applicant has failed to enter into a S106 agreement and
therefore not in compliance with Policy 94 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan
Part 1 (2024) and the Waltham Forest Supplementary Planning Document “Planning
Obligations” SPD, specifically in relation to the following planning
obligations requirements (figures applicable at the time of the assessment of
the application):A) Highways and
Transportation: i) Car Free Development - the
      development is to be classified as car-free and residents will not be
      eligible for parking permits.ii) A condition survey is required of
      the carriageway and footways fronting the site prior to the commencement
      of any works.iii) A S106 request of
      £9,000 is requested toward improving sustainable modes of transport
      including walking and cycling in the sites vicinity which will directly
      benefit new residents in this development.iv) A S106 contribution of
      £750 is requested for CLP monitoring.v) S278 works –The extent of the works will include
       but are not limited to:Renewal of the footway along the
       frontage of the site.Renewal of the access and road
       markings along the frontage of the site.B) SAMMS:i)
      SAMMS - A financial contribution of £5,850.00 towards Strategic Access
      Management and Monitoring measures (SAMMs).C) Carbon offset:Carbon
      Offset Fund (COF) contributions will be required for any shortfall in
      emission reductions, calculated to be £11,778.00D) Legal Fees:i)
      Payment of the Council’s legal fees for the preparation and completion of
      the Legal Agreement.ii)
      Monitoring Fee - A financial contribution towards the implementation and
      monitoring of and securing compliance with the S106, equal to 5% of the
      total of all other financial contributions .
